chunks: And from him (al-Hasan ibn al-Muthanna) from Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): The person in ihram plays with his beard, and a hair or two falls from it. He said: 'He gives a small amount (of food).'.

key_terms.الشَّعْرَةُ وَالِاثْنَتَانِ: A single hair and two hairs (indicating a small quantity)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or 'Umrah
key_terms.يَعْبَثُ: Plays with or fidgets with (implying casual, non-intentional removal)
key_terms.يُطْعِمُ شَيْئًا: He gives a small amount (of food as expiation)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for accidentally losing a hair from the beard while in ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the kaffarah for accidentally grooming the beard during ihram as feeding a small amount of food, reflecting the principle of proportional expiation for minor infractions. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between intentional and accidental acts, where the penalty is mitigated compared to deliberate violations, underscoring the mercy embedded in the legal framework of Hajj rituals.
